LESSON: ATHLETICS

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade six
Subject: General
Strand: Performing and Displaying
Topic 2.1: Athletics
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 15

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Athletics, part of Performing and Displaying in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade six General.

Key inquiry question: How is the jumping skill useful in athletics 2. Why is it important to maintain a tempo in athletics?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. sign vocabulary related to athletics for familiarisation,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Athletics in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. describe long jump and high jump techniques in athletics,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Athletics in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. perform the sail technique in long jump for skills acquisition,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Athletics in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. perform the scissors technique in high jump for skills acquisition,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Athletics in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. appreciate high jump and long jump techniques in athletics for enjoyment. • learners are guided to sign words related to athletics such as: long jump, high jump, long jump- sail technique, high jump- scissor style among others while seated in an appropriate seating arrangement for signing, • learners are guided to watch a virtual or live performance of a long jump and high jump, and keenly observe sail technique in long jump and scissors technique in high jump, • learners observe a demonstration of the sail technique in long jump while observing safety. 1. How is the jumping skill useful in athletics 2. Why is it important to maintain a tempo in athletics? 28 • guide learners to observe a demonstration of the scissors technique in high jump, while observing safety and rules of the game.. • in purposive groups, learners practise the sail technique in long jump accompanied by a music tempo, while observing safety . • in purposive groups, learners practise the scissors technique in high jump to a specified tempo observing safety, • learners observe each other’s performance and give feedback, • learners display and talk about own and others’ performance in long jump and high jump. note:ensure there u 29

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Athletics together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Digital literacy: The learner operates digital devices while watching performances in sail technique in the long jump and

scissors technique in the high jump.

• Creativity and Imagination: The learner practises the scissors technique and sail to a given tempo.

Values:
• Integrity: The learner displays honesty while appraising each other's performance.

• Responsibility: The learner watches videos on the performance of the long and high jumps, and practises the latter.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Safety: The learner observes safety while performing the sail technique in long jump and scissors in high jump.

Link to other learning areas:

Mathematics: is applied when the learner takes the measures of their performance and appraises accordingly.

Suggested learning resources

Found objects, fabric, coloured papers, adhesives, scissors, watercolor/ poster colours, brushes, calligraphy pens, ink, high jump

landing gear, tape measure, open places or marked fields, digital devices, whistle, long jump runway and landing area, tape

measure.
